source: paper1_isa_v5.pdf Fig. 2 and paper1_isa_supplement_v5.pdf Table S7, Fig. S6
notes: v5 reports the logging-period story over THREE measurement conditions, not the v4.1 pair. Every row carries its own condition tag.
Noise-free: finer logging is always better.
Tension-only noise: still monotonic. The optimum is at the finest 1 ms setting for EVERY excitation. Tension noise penalizes coarse logging and creates NO interior optimum.
Dual-channel noise: the interior optimum appears. It is produced by the VELOCITY channel.
Never report a pooled median over the 10 plants without the slow/fast decomposition - the pooled valley represents neither sub-group.
The word 'U-shape' is not used. The paper says 'interior optimum' and, for the pooled curve, 'pooled valley'.

series_provenance.note: Each plotted series comes from a SINGLE excitation, so the curve is internally consistent. The paper does not publish a complete noise-free E_Toggle series.

noise_free.source: supplement Table S7 NF-baseline column (complete 2-100 ms series)

tension_only.source: supplement Fig. S6(b), 50 Hz row (complete 1-100 ms series)

dual_channel.source: paper Fig. 2(a) / Section 3.4 (three published points: 5, 20 and 50 ms)

E_Toggle_noise_free_anchors.note: The only noise-free E_Toggle points the paper prints. Held here as annotations rather than as a plotted series, because two points do not make a curve.

Tlog_1ms.status: an essentially exact fit, below 0.01%; off the logarithmic axis, so Fig. 2(a) draws the noise-free curve from 2 ms onward. The point is off-scale, not missing.

Tlog_5ms.status: paper_text_exact; also the power-law anchor for the tau_min/Tlog >= 5 guideline

interior_optimum.per_excitation_note: ET1 bottoms out at 20 ms while the other excitations settle between 5 and 10 ms. The paper does not print each one individually.
interior_optimum.tension_only_note: Every excitation has its tension-only optimum at the finest 1 ms setting. Tension noise creates no interior optimum.

speed_decomposition.note: The pooled valley near 5 ms represents NEITHER sub-group. A pooled median must always be reported with this decomposition.

slow.note: Low and nearly flat, essentially insensitive to the excitation.

fast.note: Effectively unidentifiable at fine logging. Only EV1 keeps a usable optimum for these plants.

organizing_variable.name: absolute velocity-noise dose sigma_v
organizing_variable.note: sigma_v tracks the optimum's position slightly better than line speed does, but the two are structurally collinear and the margin is modest, so sigma_v ORGANIZES the trend rather than collapsing it.

tension_noise_layers: Under velocity-only noise the interior optimum is present for every excitation except ET1, so tension noise governs only ET1.
Where tension does matter it acts as a THRESHOLD on presence, not a dose: pct_T = 0.1% already sets ET1's interior optimum in 7 of 9 velocity-noise recipes, and 0.3% adds one more.

That residual ET1 dependence is confined to the fast, high-sigma_v plants: with tension noise removed entirely the five slow plants still show an interior optimum in all nine recipes; the five fast plants show none.
